newsitem.title: USA: Morrison Knudsen may buy copper mine stake.
newsitem.headline: Morrison Knudsen may buy copper mine stake.

text.p: Morrison Knudsen Corp Chairman Dennis Washington is negotiating to sell his 50.1 percent interest in the former Anaconda copper mine in Butte, Montana, to the company for about $125 million in stock.
In a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, the company said it set up a special committee of directors independent of Washington to evaluate the deal.
If completed, Washington would raise his stake in the Boise-based engineering and mining company to 50 percent from his current 37.5 percent.
The proposal is subject to approval of the committee as well as satisfaction of contractual rights of ASARCO Inc, which owns a 49.9 percent interest in the copper and molybdenum mine.
A source familiar with the deal said it was in the very early phases and was unlikely to be completed before the third quarter.
Washington bought the Anaconda Copper Co mine for $15 million in 1985, about two years after it had been shut down as unprofitable.
In 1989, after reopening the mine and turning it around, he sold the half interest to Asarco for $125 million.
